# Do consecutive success and error streaks add predictive value to deep knowledge tracing?

On ASSISTments 2015, a forecast averaging deep knowledge tracing (DKT) and a skill-history tree had the lowest next-response log loss across seven models. In 134,640 responses from 3,818 held-out learners it gained 0.00272 nats over DKT. A matched blend whose tree omitted run length and streaks recovered nearly all that gain. The remaining 0.00014 nats had a simultaneous 95% interval from −0.00008 to 0.00035. Only one of six comparisons cleared the prespecified 0.015-nat practical margin.

## Question and prior work

DKT uses a recurrent network to encode a sequence of skill–response pairs. Knowledge Tracing Machines combine learner, item, skill and accumulated practice information using factorization machines. Logistic Knowledge Tracing allows distinct functions of prior opportunities, successes and failures. Explicit practice histories and flexible skill models therefore have established precedents. Here the narrower question is whether the current run of practice on a skill, and the successes or errors at its end, give incremental information once a strong predictor already combines a recurrent history with flexible cumulative counts. The matched-blend ablation makes that increment measurable; the evidence does not establish a new tracing architecture. [DKT](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/5654-deep-knowledge-tracing) · [Knowledge Tracing Machines](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v33i01.3301750) · [Logistic Knowledge Tracing](https://doi.org/10.1109/TLT.2021.3128569)

## Design

We used the released pyKT split for the 2015 ASSISTments skill-builder data. Folds 1–4 supplied 426,288 next-response events from 12,220 training learners. Fold 0 supplied 102,776 events from 3,055 development learners. Each sequence supplied one forecast from its second event onward, conditional on observing the next skill, earlier skills and earlier responses. User IDs link records for evaluation. All three cohorts were user-disjoint. This endpoint conditions on the practice opportunities generated by the original platform. It cannot identify the causal effect of encouraging a learner to continue a streak. [Dataset publisher](https://sites.google.com/site/assistmentsdata/datasets/2015-assistments-skill-builder-data) · [pyKT release and benchmark](https://github.com/pykt-team/pykt-toolkit/tree/ccbaf37b07e3e7ff7b2415475b2faacb967d54ea)

For DKT we ran the pyKT implementation of the Piech et al. architecture. Every learner's history starts at its first recorded event. The recurrent state at the previous event forecasts the current skill. A 64-dimensional LSTM trained for up to 12 epochs, with development loss selecting epoch 9. The history trees received current skill, success and failure counts for learner and skill, total opportunities, last same-skill response and distance since that response. The full tree also receives same-skill run length and the consecutive successes and failures within that run. These features reset upon a skill change. Each tree selects its own leaf budget using development loss. The short and full blends independently selected equal recurrent and tree weights. Skill priors use training outcomes only. [Frozen protocol](protocol.md) · [Development scores](run/development.json) · [Upstream DKT implementation](https://github.com/pykt-team/pykt-toolkit/blob/ccbaf37b07e3e7ff7b2415475b2faacb967d54ea/pykt/models/dkt.py)

## Results on the released user holdout

There were 98,733 correct responses. Each event contributed equally to negative log likelihood. Paired intervals resampled whole learners 5,000 times using a common bootstrap sample for every model, with Bonferroni percentile endpoints across six comparisons. They condition on the fitted models and the observed platform. [All numerical results](run/result.json) · [Per-event predictions](run/predictions.csv.gz)

| Forecast | NLL | Gain from full blend | Simultaneous 95% interval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Training skill rate | .55507 | .04299 | [.04017, .04605] |
| Full-history logistic regression | .52426 | .01218 | [.01102, .01338] |
| DKT | .51480 | .00272 | [.00204, .00343] |
| Full-history tree | .51658 | .00449 | [.00386, .00512] |
| Tree without streaks | .51700 | .00492 | [.00424, .00562] |
| DKT + tree without streaks | .51222 | .00014 | [−.00008, .00035] |
| DKT + full-history tree | .51208 | — | — |

Selecting both blend weights on development data allowed the shorter history representation to compete on equal terms. The result supports a small benefit from combining recurrent and cumulative-history predictions. The observed incremental value of explicit streaks is compatible with zero. Because the candidate failed the first stage, the protocol ended before a simpleKT, HawkesKT, LêFoKT or second-dataset challenge. This study contributes zero papers to the portfolio's all-baseline count.

## Reproduction

The data and pyKT DKT code are SHA-256 checked at runtime. The fit used Python on a CUDA-enabled RTX 4060 Ti with PyTorch 2.6.0+cu124, scikit-learn 1.9.1 and pandas 2.3.3. The predictor uses scikit-learn trees and pyKT's open-source DKT model, trained from scratch. Exact GPU retraining across different drivers or versions can vary. The Node verifier reconstructs the held-out labels, disjoint learner IDs, blend equations and seven log losses from 942,480 saved forecasts. Two regression tests check response cutoff and target indexing. Earlier outcomes remain available within test learners' histories as they accumulate.

```bash
set -eu
e=research_v4_2/external/knowledge_tracing
r=private_data/raw/assist2015
o=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$r"
base=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pykt-team/pykt-toolkit/ccbaf37b07e3e7ff7b2415475b2faacb967d54ea
for f in train_valid.csv test.csv; do curl -fsSL "$base/data/assist2015/$f" -o "$r/$f"; done
curl -fsSL "$base/pykt/models/dkt.py" -o "$r/dkt.py"
(cd "$e" && sha256sum -c protocol.sha256 && python test_history.py)
node --check "$e/verify.mjs"
node "$e/verify.mjs" "$r" "$e/run"
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 python "$e/study.py" "$r" "$o"
node "$e/verify.mjs" "$r" "$o"
```
